Phase 7 · Session 73

Capstone: legacy migration, part 1

Move a messy export from an old system into a clean, constrained schema: profile it, write the cleaning functions, quarantine what cannot be trusted, and prove nothing was lost.

Topics

The situation

A small shop is replacing its old order system. The old system keeps everything in one table, legacy_sales: one row per order line, with the customer typed in again on every line, dates and amounts stored as text, and one-letter status codes. The new schema shop has customers, orders and order lines with real types and constraints. The old app must keep working while you migrate (that is part 2, Session 74).

CREATE TABLE legacy_sales (           -- one row per order line, exported from the old shop system
  line_no    int PRIMARY KEY,
  order_ref  text,
  cust_name  text,
  cust_email text,
  order_date text,                     -- usually DD/MM/YYYY
  status     char(1),                  -- P pending, S shipped, D delivered, C cancelled
  sku        text,
  qty        text,
  amount     text                      -- line total, with thousands separators
);

The plan

  • Profile before you write any migration: counts, distinct values, formats. Every surprise you find now is a failed migration you do not have to debug later.
  • Clean with small IMMUTABLE functions (parse_legacy_date, parse_amount, parse_qty, norm_email, legacy_status) that return NULL for anything they cannot read. They can be tested one by one and reused by the dual-write trigger in part 2.
  • Quarantine, do not guess. Rows with problems go to shop.migration_errors with the reasons; a person decides. An order migrates only if every one of its lines is clean.
  • Idempotent: every INSERT has ON CONFLICT … DO NOTHING on a key from the old system (legacy_ref, legacy_line_no), so the migration can be run again after a fix.
  • Reconcile: migrated + quarantined = everything, and the money adds up.

Each question below starts from a fresh database, so the answers repeat the setup (legacy table, functions, schema). In your own psql session, run each piece once and keep going.

Questions

Write your answers in psql/s73.sql and run them on the practice database. Open an answer only after you have tried.

CREATE FUNCTION parse_legacy_date(v text) RETURNS date
LANGUAGE plpgsql IMMUTABLE AS $$
BEGIN
  IF v ~ '^\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4}$' THEN
    RETURN to_date(v, 'DD/MM/YYYY');
  ELSIF v ~ '^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$' THEN
    RETURN v::date;
  END IF;
  RETURN NULL;
EXCEPTION WHEN data_exception THEN          -- e.g. 31/02/2026
  RETURN NULL;
END;
$$;

CREATE FUNCTION parse_amount(v text) RETURNS numeric
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE
RETURN NULLIF(regexp_replace(v, '[^0-9.]', '', 'g'), '')::numeric(10, 2);

CREATE FUNCTION parse_qty(v text) RETURNS int
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE
RETURN CASE WHEN v ~ '^\d+$' THEN v::int END;

CREATE FUNCTION norm_email(v text) RETURNS text
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE
RETURN NULLIF(lower(trim(v)), '');

CREATE FUNCTION legacy_status(c char) RETURNS text
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE
RETURN CASE c WHEN 'P' THEN 'pending' WHEN 'S' THEN 'shipped' WHEN 'D' THEN 'delivered' WHEN 'C' THEN 'cancelled' END;

CREATE FUNCTION parse_legacy_date(v text) RETURNS date
LANGUAGE plpgsql IMMUTABLE AS $$
BEGIN
  IF v ~ '^\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4}$' THEN
    RETURN to_date(v, 'DD/MM/YYYY');
  ELSIF v ~ '^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$' THEN
    RETURN v::date;
  END IF;
  RETURN NULL;
EXCEPTION WHEN data_exception THEN          -- e.g. 31/02/2026
  RETURN NULL;
END;
$$;

CREATE FUNCTION parse_amount(v text) RETURNS numeric
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE
RETURN NULLIF(regexp_replace(v, '[^0-9.]', '', 'g'), '')::numeric(10, 2);

CREATE FUNCTION parse_qty(v text) RETURNS int
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE
RETURN CASE WHEN v ~ '^\d+$' THEN v::int END;

CREATE FUNCTION norm_email(v text) RETURNS text
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE
RETURN NULLIF(lower(trim(v)), '');

CREATE FUNCTION legacy_status(c char) RETURNS text
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE
RETURN CASE c WHEN 'P' THEN 'pending' WHEN 'S' THEN 'shipped' WHEN 'D' THEN 'delivered' WHEN 'C' THEN 'cancelled' END;

CREATE VIEW legacy_problems AS
SELECT line_no, order_ref, problems
FROM (
  SELECT line_no, order_ref, array_remove(ARRAY[
           CASE WHEN parse_legacy_date(order_date) IS NULL THEN 'bad date' END,
           CASE WHEN norm_email(cust_email) IS NULL THEN 'no email' END,
           CASE WHEN legacy_status(status) IS NULL THEN 'unknown status' END,
           CASE WHEN parse_qty(qty) IS NULL OR parse_qty(qty) = 0 THEN 'bad quantity' END,
           CASE WHEN parse_amount(amount) IS NULL THEN 'bad amount' END
         ], NULL) AS problems
  FROM legacy_sales
) p
WHERE cardinality(problems) > 0;

  6. Create the new schema (code in the answer). Then insert directly: a customer with an upper-case email, the same customer in lower case, an order for customer 1, the same order looked up by email, and a line with quantity 0.

    Compare your output with the answer

    Answer
    CREATE SCHEMA shop;

CREATE TABLE shop.customers (
  customer_id int GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  email       text NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (email = lower(email)),
  full_name   text NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE shop.orders (
  order_id    int GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  legacy_ref  text UNIQUE,                 -- ORD-1001: keeps the link to the old system
  customer_id int NOT NULL REFERENCES shop.customers,
  order_date  date NOT NULL,
  status      text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled'))
);
CREATE INDEX ON shop.orders (customer_id);
CREATE TABLE shop.order_lines (
  order_id       int NOT NULL REFERENCES shop.orders,
  sku            text NOT NULL,
  qty            int NOT NULL CHECK (qty > 0),
  amount         numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (amount >= 0),
  legacy_line_no int UNIQUE,
  PRIMARY KEY (order_id, sku)
);
CREATE TABLE shop.migration_errors (
  line_no  int PRIMARY KEY,
  problems text[] NOT NULL,
  noted_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

practice=# INSERT INTO shop.order_lines (order_id, sku, qty, amount) SELECT order_id, 'MUG', 0, 0 FROM shop.orders WHERE legacy_ref = 'TEST';
ERROR:  new row for relation "order_lines" violates check constraint "order_lines_qty_check"
DETAIL:  Failing row contains (2, MUG, 0, 0.00, null).

    Both bad rows are rejected by CHECK constraints. And a surprise on the way: the order for customer 1 fails, because the good customer got id 2. The rejected insert had already used id 1, and identity values are never given back. Never hard-code generated ids; look them up by a natural key. The constraints are the real migration spec: whatever the cleaning functions miss, the new schema refuses. Write them first, then make the data fit, never the other way round.

CREATE FUNCTION parse_legacy_date(v text) RETURNS date
LANGUAGE plpgsql IMMUTABLE AS $$
BEGIN
  IF v ~ '^\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4}$' THEN
    RETURN to_date(v, 'DD/MM/YYYY');
  ELSIF v ~ '^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$' THEN
    RETURN v::date;
  END IF;
  RETURN NULL;
EXCEPTION WHEN data_exception THEN          -- e.g. 31/02/2026
  RETURN NULL;
END;
$$;

CREATE FUNCTION parse_amount(v text) RETURNS numeric
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE
RETURN NULLIF(regexp_replace(v, '[^0-9.]', '', 'g'), '')::numeric(10, 2);

CREATE FUNCTION parse_qty(v text) RETURNS int
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE
RETURN CASE WHEN v ~ '^\d+$' THEN v::int END;

CREATE FUNCTION norm_email(v text) RETURNS text
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE
RETURN NULLIF(lower(trim(v)), '');

CREATE FUNCTION legacy_status(c char) RETURNS text
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE
RETURN CASE c WHEN 'P' THEN 'pending' WHEN 'S' THEN 'shipped' WHEN 'D' THEN 'delivered' WHEN 'C' THEN 'cancelled' END;

CREATE VIEW legacy_problems AS
SELECT line_no, order_ref, problems
FROM (
  SELECT line_no, order_ref, array_remove(ARRAY[
           CASE WHEN parse_legacy_date(order_date) IS NULL THEN 'bad date' END,
           CASE WHEN norm_email(cust_email) IS NULL THEN 'no email' END,
           CASE WHEN legacy_status(status) IS NULL THEN 'unknown status' END,
           CASE WHEN parse_qty(qty) IS NULL OR parse_qty(qty) = 0 THEN 'bad quantity' END,
           CASE WHEN parse_amount(amount) IS NULL THEN 'bad amount' END
         ], NULL) AS problems
  FROM legacy_sales
) p
WHERE cardinality(problems) > 0;
CREATE SCHEMA shop;

CREATE TABLE shop.customers (
  customer_id int GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  email       text NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (email = lower(email)),
  full_name   text NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE shop.orders (
  order_id    int GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  legacy_ref  text UNIQUE,                 -- ORD-1001: keeps the link to the old system
  customer_id int NOT NULL REFERENCES shop.customers,
  order_date  date NOT NULL,
  status      text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled'))
);
CREATE INDEX ON shop.orders (customer_id);
CREATE TABLE shop.order_lines (
  order_id       int NOT NULL REFERENCES shop.orders,
  sku            text NOT NULL,
  qty            int NOT NULL CHECK (qty > 0),
  amount         numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (amount >= 0),
  legacy_line_no int UNIQUE,
  PRIMARY KEY (order_id, sku)
);
CREATE TABLE shop.migration_errors (
  line_no  int PRIMARY KEY,
  problems text[] NOT NULL,
  noted_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
INSERT INTO shop.customers (email, full_name)

FROM legacy_sales
WHERE norm_email(cust_email) IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY norm_email(cust_email), line_no
ON CONFLICT (email) DO NOTHING;
INSERT INTO shop.orders (legacy_ref, customer_id, order_date, status)
SELECT DISTINCT ON (l.order_ref) l.order_ref, c.customer_id, parse_legacy_date(l.order_date), legacy_status(l.status)
FROM legacy_sales l
JOIN shop.customers c ON c.email = norm_email(l.cust_email)
WHERE l.order_ref NOT IN (SELECT order_ref FROM legacy_problems)
ORDER BY l.order_ref, l.line_no
ON CONFLICT (legacy_ref) DO NOTHING;
INSERT INTO shop.order_lines (order_id, sku, qty, amount, legacy_line_no)
SELECT o.order_id, l.sku, parse_qty(l.qty), parse_amount(l.amount), l.line_no
FROM legacy_sales l
JOIN shop.orders o ON o.legacy_ref = l.order_ref
ON CONFLICT (legacy_line_no) DO NOTHING;
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM shop.orders) AS orders, (SELECT count(*) FROM shop.order_lines) AS lines;

CREATE FUNCTION parse_legacy_date(v text) RETURNS date
LANGUAGE plpgsql IMMUTABLE AS $$
BEGIN
  IF v ~ '^\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4}$' THEN
    RETURN to_date(v, 'DD/MM/YYYY');
  ELSIF v ~ '^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$' THEN
    RETURN v::date;
  END IF;
  RETURN NULL;
EXCEPTION WHEN data_exception THEN          -- e.g. 31/02/2026
  RETURN NULL;
END;
$$;

CREATE FUNCTION parse_amount(v text) RETURNS numeric
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE
RETURN NULLIF(regexp_replace(v, '[^0-9.]', '', 'g'), '')::numeric(10, 2);

CREATE FUNCTION parse_qty(v text) RETURNS int
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE
RETURN CASE WHEN v ~ '^\d+$' THEN v::int END;

CREATE FUNCTION norm_email(v text) RETURNS text
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE
RETURN NULLIF(lower(trim(v)), '');

CREATE FUNCTION legacy_status(c char) RETURNS text
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE
RETURN CASE c WHEN 'P' THEN 'pending' WHEN 'S' THEN 'shipped' WHEN 'D' THEN 'delivered' WHEN 'C' THEN 'cancelled' END;

CREATE VIEW legacy_problems AS
SELECT line_no, order_ref, problems
FROM (
  SELECT line_no, order_ref, array_remove(ARRAY[
           CASE WHEN parse_legacy_date(order_date) IS NULL THEN 'bad date' END,
           CASE WHEN norm_email(cust_email) IS NULL THEN 'no email' END,
           CASE WHEN legacy_status(status) IS NULL THEN 'unknown status' END,
           CASE WHEN parse_qty(qty) IS NULL OR parse_qty(qty) = 0 THEN 'bad quantity' END,
           CASE WHEN parse_amount(amount) IS NULL THEN 'bad amount' END
         ], NULL) AS problems
  FROM legacy_sales
) p
WHERE cardinality(problems) > 0;
CREATE SCHEMA shop;

CREATE TABLE shop.customers (
  customer_id int GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  email       text NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (email = lower(email)),
  full_name   text NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE shop.orders (
  order_id    int GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  legacy_ref  text UNIQUE,                 -- ORD-1001: keeps the link to the old system
  customer_id int NOT NULL REFERENCES shop.customers,
  order_date  date NOT NULL,
  status      text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled'))
);
CREATE INDEX ON shop.orders (customer_id);
CREATE TABLE shop.order_lines (
  order_id       int NOT NULL REFERENCES shop.orders,
  sku            text NOT NULL,
  qty            int NOT NULL CHECK (qty > 0),
  amount         numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (amount >= 0),
  legacy_line_no int UNIQUE,
  PRIMARY KEY (order_id, sku)
);
CREATE TABLE shop.migration_errors (
  line_no  int PRIMARY KEY,
  problems text[] NOT NULL,
  noted_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

  legacy_ref  text UNIQUE,                 -- ORD-1001: keeps the link to the old system
  customer_id int NOT NULL REFERENCES shop.customers,
  order_date  date NOT NULL,
  status      text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled'))
);
CREATE INDEX ON shop.orders (customer_id);
CREATE TABLE shop.order_lines (
  order_id       int NOT NULL REFERENCES shop.orders,
  sku            text NOT NULL,
  qty            int NOT NULL CHECK (qty > 0),
  amount         numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (amount >= 0),
  legacy_line_no int UNIQUE,
  PRIMARY KEY (order_id, sku)
);
CREATE TABLE shop.migration_errors (
  line_no  int PRIMARY KEY,
  problems text[] NOT NULL,
  noted_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE PROCEDURE migrate_legacy()
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
  n bigint;
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO shop.customers (email, full_name)
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (norm_email(cust_email)) norm_email(cust_email), trim(cust_name)
  FROM legacy_sales
  WHERE norm_email(cust_email) IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY norm_email(cust_email), line_no
  ON CONFLICT (email) DO NOTHING;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS n = ROW_COUNT;
  RAISE NOTICE 'customers: %', n;

  INSERT INTO shop.orders (legacy_ref, customer_id, order_date, status)
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (l.order_ref) l.order_ref, c.customer_id, parse_legacy_date(l.order_date), legacy_status(l.status)
  FROM legacy_sales l
  JOIN shop.customers c ON c.email = norm_email(l.cust_email)
  WHERE l.order_ref NOT IN (SELECT order_ref FROM legacy_problems)
  ORDER BY l.order_ref, l.line_no
  ON CONFLICT (legacy_ref) DO NOTHING;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS n = ROW_COUNT;
  RAISE NOTICE 'orders: %', n;

  INSERT INTO shop.order_lines (order_id, sku, qty, amount, legacy_line_no)
  SELECT o.order_id, l.sku, parse_qty(l.qty), parse_amount(l.amount), l.line_no
  FROM legacy_sales l
  JOIN shop.orders o ON o.legacy_ref = l.order_ref
  ON CONFLICT (legacy_line_no) DO NOTHING;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS n = ROW_COUNT;
  RAISE NOTICE 'lines: %', n;

  INSERT INTO shop.migration_errors (line_no, problems)
  SELECT line_no, problems FROM legacy_problems
  ON CONFLICT (line_no) DO NOTHING;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS n = ROW_COUNT;
  RAISE NOTICE 'quarantined: %', n;

  COMMIT;
END;
$$;
CALL migrate_legacy();
CALL migrate_legacy();

practice=# CREATE FUNCTION parse_legacy_date(v text) RETURNS date
           LANGUAGE plpgsql IMMUTABLE AS $$
           BEGIN
             IF v ~ '^\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4}$' THEN
               RETURN to_date(v, 'DD/MM/YYYY');
             ELSIF v ~ '^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$' THEN
               RETURN v::date;
             END IF;
             RETURN NULL;
           EXCEPTION WHEN data_exception THEN          -- e.g. 31/02/2026
             RETURN NULL;
           END;
           $$;

           CREATE FUNCTION parse_amount(v text) RETURNS numeric
           LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE
           RETURN NULLIF(regexp_replace(v, '[^0-9.]', '', 'g'), '')::numeric(10, 2);

           CREATE FUNCTION parse_qty(v text) RETURNS int
           LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE
           RETURN CASE WHEN v ~ '^\d+$' THEN v::int END;

           CREATE FUNCTION norm_email(v text) RETURNS text
           LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE
           RETURN NULLIF(lower(trim(v)), '');

           CREATE FUNCTION legacy_status(c char) RETURNS text
           LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE
           RETURN CASE c WHEN 'P' THEN 'pending' WHEN 'S' THEN 'shipped' WHEN 'D' THEN 'delivered' WHEN 'C' THEN 'cancelled' END;

           CREATE VIEW legacy_problems AS
           SELECT line_no, order_ref, problems
           FROM (
             SELECT line_no, order_ref, array_remove(ARRAY[
                      CASE WHEN parse_legacy_date(order_date) IS NULL THEN 'bad date' END,
                      CASE WHEN norm_email(cust_email) IS NULL THEN 'no email' END,
                      CASE WHEN legacy_status(status) IS NULL THEN 'unknown status' END,
                      CASE WHEN parse_qty(qty) IS NULL OR parse_qty(qty) = 0 THEN 'bad quantity' END,
                      CASE WHEN parse_amount(amount) IS NULL THEN 'bad amount' END
                    ], NULL) AS problems
             FROM legacy_sales
           ) p
           WHERE cardinality(problems) > 0;

← Phase 7: Functions, triggers + RLSAll phasesSchema

Phase 7 · Session 74

Capstone: legacy migration, part 2

Keep the old and the new schema in step while the old app is still in use, give the old app a compatible view, switch over in one short transaction, and know how to switch back.

Topics

Where we are

Session 73 left a clean shop schema with 6 orders and 8 lines, 4 lines in quarantine, and an idempotent migration. Every question below starts from that state (the answers run Session 73's migration as a hidden setup step; in your own psql, just continue from Session 73's challenge).

The cut-over plan

1. Dual write     a trigger on legacy_sales copies every new or changed line into shop     (Q2–Q4)
2. Compatibility  a view with the old columns, built on shop, writable via INSTEAD OF  (Q5–Q6)
3. Switch         one short transaction: rename the table away, the view in its place  (Q7)
4. Lock down      the old app may only use the view                                    (Q8)
5. Way back       a tested script that copies new rows back and swaps the names       (challenge)

The old app never changes: it keeps sending INSERT INTO legacy_sales …. Before the switch that hits the table (and the trigger copies it); after the switch it hits the view (and the INSTEAD OF trigger writes to shop). That is the "expand, migrate, contract" pattern from Session 61, applied to a whole table.

During dual write, the old system is still the truth, so the trigger must never make an old-app write fail: a bad line goes to quarantine instead (Q3). After the switch, the new schema is the truth, and bad data is rejected outright (Q6). Decide which side is the truth at every step, and write it down.

Questions

Write your answers in psql/s74.sql and run them on the practice database. Open an answer only after you have tried.

  1. Reconcile per order: compare each migrated order's total in shop with the total of the same order's lines in legacy_sales. List the orders that differ.

    Compare your output with the answer

    Answer
    WITH old AS (
  SELECT order_ref, sum(parse_amount(amount)) AS total FROM legacy_sales GROUP BY order_ref
), new AS (
  SELECT o.legacy_ref, sum(l.amount) AS total
  FROM shop.orders o JOIN shop.order_lines l ON l.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY o.legacy_ref
)
SELECT new.legacy_ref, old.total AS legacy_total, new.total AS shop_total
FROM new JOIN old ON old.order_ref = new.legacy_ref
WHERE old.total IS DISTINCT FROM new.total;
SELECT count(*) AS orders_checked FROM shop.orders;

    No order differs (0 rows), and 6 orders were checked. Session 73 compared the grand total; per-order checks catch a line attached to the wrong order, which a grand total cannot. Keep this query: it runs again after the switch.

  2. Dual write: create the sync_legacy() trigger on legacy_sales (code in the answer). The old app then inserts a line for a new customer: line 13, ORD-1011, Tara Sen, tara@mail.test, 08/02/2026, P, CAP, 1, 599.00. Does it appear in shop?

    Compare your output with the answer

    Answer
    CREATE FUNCTION sync_legacy() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
  v_problems text[];
BEGIN
  SELECT problems INTO v_problems FROM legacy_problems WHERE line_no = NEW.line_no;
  IF FOUND THEN                                     -- not clean: quarantine, do not migrate
    INSERT INTO shop.migration_errors (line_no, problems) VALUES (NEW.line_no, v_problems)
    ON CONFLICT (line_no) DO UPDATE SET problems = EXCLUDED.problems, noted_at = now();
    RETURN NULL;
  END IF;
  BEGIN
    INSERT INTO shop.customers (email, full_name) VALUES (norm_email(NEW.cust_email), trim(NEW.cust_name))
    ON CONFLICT (email) DO NOTHING;
    INSERT INTO shop.orders (legacy_ref, customer_id, order_date, status)
    SELECT NEW.order_ref, customer_id, parse_legacy_date(NEW.order_date), legacy_status(NEW.status)
    FROM shop.customers WHERE email = norm_email(NEW.cust_email)
    ON CONFLICT (legacy_ref) DO UPDATE SET order_date = EXCLUDED.order_date, status = EXCLUDED.status;
    INSERT INTO shop.order_lines (order_id, sku, qty, amount, legacy_line_no)
    SELECT order_id, NEW.sku, parse_qty(NEW.qty), parse_amount(NEW.amount), NEW.line_no
    FROM shop.orders WHERE legacy_ref = NEW.order_ref
    ON CONFLICT (legacy_line_no) DO UPDATE SET sku = EXCLUDED.sku, qty = EXCLUDED.qty, amount = EXCLUDED.amount;
    DELETE FROM shop.migration_errors WHERE line_no = NEW.line_no;
  EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN                        -- never break the old app: quarantine instead
    INSERT INTO shop.migration_errors (line_no, problems) VALUES (NEW.line_no, ARRAY[SQLERRM])
    ON CONFLICT (line_no) DO UPDATE SET problems = EXCLUDED.problems, noted_at = now();
  END;
  RETURN NULL;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER legacy_sync AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON legacy_sales
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_legacy();

    CREATE FUNCTION sync_legacy() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
  v_problems text[];
BEGIN
  SELECT problems INTO v_problems FROM legacy_problems WHERE line_no = NEW.line_no;
  IF FOUND THEN                                     -- not clean: quarantine, do not migrate
    INSERT INTO shop.migration_errors (line_no, problems) VALUES (NEW.line_no, v_problems)
    ON CONFLICT (line_no) DO UPDATE SET problems = EXCLUDED.problems, noted_at = now();
    RETURN NULL;
  END IF;
  BEGIN
    INSERT INTO shop.customers (email, full_name) VALUES (norm_email(NEW.cust_email), trim(NEW.cust_name))
    ON CONFLICT (email) DO NOTHING;
    INSERT INTO shop.orders (legacy_ref, customer_id, order_date, status)
    SELECT NEW.order_ref, customer_id, parse_legacy_date(NEW.order_date), legacy_status(NEW.status)
    FROM shop.customers WHERE email = norm_email(NEW.cust_email)
    ON CONFLICT (legacy_ref) DO UPDATE SET order_date = EXCLUDED.order_date, status = EXCLUDED.status;
    INSERT INTO shop.order_lines (order_id, sku, qty, amount, legacy_line_no)
    SELECT order_id, NEW.sku, parse_qty(NEW.qty), parse_amount(NEW.amount), NEW.line_no
    FROM shop.orders WHERE legacy_ref = NEW.order_ref
    ON CONFLICT (legacy_line_no) DO UPDATE SET sku = EXCLUDED.sku, qty = EXCLUDED.qty, amount = EXCLUDED.amount;
    DELETE FROM shop.migration_errors WHERE line_no = NEW.line_no;
  EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN                        -- never break the old app: quarantine instead
    INSERT INTO shop.migration_errors (line_no, problems) VALUES (NEW.line_no, ARRAY[SQLERRM])
    ON CONFLICT (line_no) DO UPDATE SET problems = EXCLUDED.problems, noted_at = now();
  END;
  RETURN NULL;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER legacy_sync AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON legacy_sales
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_legacy();

  6. Make the view writable for the old app: add the INSTEAD OF INSERT trigger legacy_view_insert (code in the answer; after the switch, bad lines are rejected, not quarantined). Insert a good line and a line with quantity '0x' through the view.

    Compare your output with the answer

    Answer
    CREATE VIEW shop.legacy_sales_v AS
SELECT l.legacy_line_no                         AS line_no,
       o.legacy_ref                             AS order_ref,
       c.full_name                              AS cust_name,
       c.email                                  AS cust_email,
       to_char(o.order_date, 'DD/MM/YYYY')      AS order_date,
       (CASE o.status WHEN 'pending' THEN 'P' WHEN 'shipped' THEN 'S'
                      WHEN 'delivered' THEN 'D' WHEN 'cancelled' THEN 'C' END)::char(1) AS status,
       l.sku,
       l.qty::text                              AS qty,
       to_char(l.amount, 'FM9,999,990.00')      AS amount
FROM shop.order_lines l
JOIN shop.orders o    ON o.order_id = l.order_id
JOIN shop.customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;
CREATE FUNCTION legacy_view_insert() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
BEGIN
  IF parse_legacy_date(NEW.order_date) IS NULL OR legacy_status(NEW.status) IS NULL
     OR parse_qty(NEW.qty) IS NULL OR parse_amount(NEW.amount) IS NULL OR norm_email(NEW.cust_email) IS NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'order line % rejected', NEW.line_no USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation',
      DETAIL = format('date %L, status %L, qty %L, amount %L, email %L',
                      NEW.order_date, NEW.status, NEW.qty, NEW.amount, NEW.cust_email);
  END IF;
  INSERT INTO shop.customers (email, full_name) VALUES (norm_email(NEW.cust_email), trim(NEW.cust_name))
  ON CONFLICT (email) DO NOTHING;
  INSERT INTO shop.orders (legacy_ref, customer_id, order_date, status)
  SELECT NEW.order_ref, customer_id, parse_legacy_date(NEW.order_date), legacy_status(NEW.status)
  FROM shop.customers WHERE email = norm_email(NEW.cust_email)
  ON CONFLICT (legacy_ref) DO NOTHING;
  INSERT INTO shop.order_lines (order_id, sku, qty, amount, legacy_line_no)
  SELECT order_id, NEW.sku, parse_qty(NEW.qty), parse_amount(NEW.amount), NEW.line_no
  FROM shop.orders WHERE legacy_ref = NEW.order_ref;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER legacy_view_insert INSTEAD OF INSERT ON shop.legacy_sales_v
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION legacy_view_insert();
